profile.stagger_pattern: Two three-seat council classes plus the mayor. Class 1 seats (labeled At-Large Seat A/B/C here) are elected in 2018, 2022, 2026. Class 2 seats (At-Large Seat D/E/F) plus the directly elected Mayor are elected in 2016, 2020, 2024. Elections are held in the fall of even-numbered years: an August primary (moved to the second-to-last Tuesday in July from 2026 onward) at which a candidate receiving a majority of votes cast is declared elected outright effective as of the general election date, and a November general/runoff only for seats not decided in the primary. Unexpired terms created by mid-term vacancies are filled by council appointment until the next regular election, at which the remainder is filled by ballot as a short-term seat (e.g. the two-year council term on the 2020 ballot).

run_log.detail: Registry lists Yavapai County as 'unresolved - DNS failure and robots timeout'. Re-tested. yavapaiaz.gov (the county's general host) returns HTTP 403 to curl with a browser UA on every path including /robots.txt. The actual elections host is a DIFFERENT domain, yavapaivotes.gov, which publishes canvass PDFs at /files/assets/elections/v/1/documents/results/{year}/{slug}.pdf - but it also returns 403 to both curl (browser UA) and WebFetch. Yavapai should be reclassified from 'unresolved' to 'blocked (403 to all fetchers, both hosts)', with yavapaivotes.gov recorded as the correct elections host for anyone with a browser-capable tool. Same finding applies to Chino Valley.

Registry warning honoured: did not attempt cottonwood.suiteonemedia.com. journalaz.com (Verde Independent / Larson Newspapers) verified fetchable by plain curl including its ?s= site search, and carried by far the highest-yield material for this city. verdenews.com also returns 200.

Structural question SETTLED from the city's own pages rather than the municipal code (library.municode.com/az/cottonwood exists and returns 200, but the city site answered in fewer calls). cottonwoodaz.gov/785/Elections-Information: 'Cottonwood's legislative body - the Cottonwood City Council - consists of one Mayor and six Council Members. These officials serve staggered four-year terms, and are elected through non-partisan, at-large elections. City elections are held in the fall of each even-numbered year.' cottonwoodaz.gov/151/City-Council: 'The Mayor is directly elected to a four-year term. The Council Members are elected for four-year staggered terms. The Council designates one of its members as Vice Mayor, who serves at the pleasure at the Council.' So: 7 seats, 4-year staggered terms, at-large non-partisan, MAYOR DIRECTLY ELECTED (not council-selected), Vice Mayor council-designated from among members.

A.R.S. 9-821.01(D) trap CONFIRMED ADOPTED by Cottonwood, verbatim from the elections page: 'A candidate for City office who receives a majority of all votes cast at the primary election shall be declared elected, effective as of the date of the general election... If no candidate receives a majority of the votes cast in the primary election, or if the number of seats to be filled exceeds the number of candidates who receive a majority of votes cast, a runoff election will be held on the day of the general election.' This is load-bearing: the 2018 (all 3 seats), 2020 (all seats) and 2024 (mayor + 2 of 3 council seats) races were decided in the AUGUST/JULY primary and never appeared on a November ballot. Also recorded: AZ moved its primary permanently to the second-to-last Tuesday in July by a bill signed 2026-02-06, so the 2026 Cottonwood primary was 2026-07-21, not 2026-08-04.

Rung 1/2 (county portal / canvass) dead: yavapaivotes.gov 403 to curl and to WebFetch. No county canvass PDF obtained. Routed to rung 4 (newspaper) and to the ACFR route instead; every cycle was recovered.

ACFR ROUTE IS THE SPINE FOR THIS CITY and gave an unbroken annual officials series. CivicPlus Archive Center: https://www.cottonwoodaz.gov/Archive.aspx?AMID=37 lists the whole ACFR series back to FY2000; https://www.cottonwoodaz.gov/Archive.aspx?ADID={id} returns the PDF directly to curl (WebFetch not needed). ADID map: 488=FY2018, 529=FY2019, 559=FY2020, 583=FY2021, 602=FY2022, 611=FY2023, 616=FY2024, 621=FY2025. Every one has an introductory-section 'Principal Officials as of June 30, {year}' page naming the Mayor, the Vice Mayor by name, and all five remaining council members. Extracted locally with pdftotext -layout. Eight independent annual snapshots; the reconstructed seat model reproduces all eight exactly.

CENSUS CORRECTION - the AgendaCenter finding in the input workbook is wrong for this city. cottonwoodaz.gov/AgendaCenter is real and its dated search endpoint works (/AgendaCenter/Search/?term=&CIDs=2,3,...,13&startDate=&endDate= enumerates 2013-2026, so 2023 and 2025 are NOT missing - the census's year list was a browse artifact of the default category). BUT the AgendaCenter contains ONLY boards and commissions (cat2-cat13: Airport Commission, Board of Adjustment, Historic Preservation, IDA, Library Advisory, Municipal Property Corp, Parks & Rec, Personnel Board, P&Z, Public Safety Personnel Board, Youth Advisory). There is no City Council category; CIDs=1 returns nothing. Verified by pulling AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_03062019-510 and _12042019-590, both of which are Airport Commission minutes. CITY COUNCIL agendas and minutes live on two other systems linked from /129/Agendas-Minutes: cottonwoodaz.granicus.com/ViewPublisher.php?view_id=1 (fetchable by curl; council minutes as https://cottonwoodaz.granicus.com/services/minutes/reports/{uuid}/attachment PDFs, archive reaches back to Oct 2021) and cottonwood.novusagenda.com/agendapublic/ for the earlier period (ASP.NET postback search, not driven within budget). Used the Granicus 2022-01-04 council minutes roll call as an independent check on the FY2021/FY2022 ACFR.

SEVEN mid-term changes found, all dated from journalaz.com articles fetched and read in full text (not from search snippets): (1) Vice Mayor Kyla Allen announced 2019-01-15 she would step down effective 2019-02-28 (moved outside city limits, residency requirement); council accepted the resignation 2019-02-05. (2) Jackie Nairn appointed 2019-03-07 at a special meeting, sworn in Monday 2019-03-11, 'to take her position on the Cottonwood City Council until 2020'. (3) Deb Althouse stepped down 2019-10-31; council interviewed Carol Conti, Jesse Dowling and Debbie Wilden, chose Wilden 4-2 (Mathews and Jauregui dissenting); Wilden took the oath Friday 2019-12-06. (4) Tosca Henry resigned effective Friday 2023-03-31, confirmed by Deputy City Clerk Tami Mayes. (5) Derek Palosaari appointed unanimously 2023-05-22, took office 2023-06-06. (6) Jackie Nairn resigned (moved to Buckeye) in autumn 2023; Michael Mathews appointed 2023-12-12 by 4-2 after an earlier 3-3 failure. (7) Lisa DuVernay RECALLED at the 2024-11-05 general election and replaced by Christopher Dowell (66%-33%), the ballot citing conduct at 2023-08-08 and 2023-10-03 council meetings. Also: Lindsay Masten withdrew 2024-08-14 from the November runoff for the third 2024 council seat, handing it to Joy Mosley.

Day-of-week checks pass: 2018-08-28 Tue, 2019-03-11 Mon ('sworn in ... on Monday, March 11' - matches), 2019-12-06 Fri ('On Friday, Dec. 6' - matches), 2020-08-04 Tue, 2022-08-02 Tue, 2023-03-31 Fri ('effective Friday, March 31' - matches), 2023-12-12 Tue ('special meeting on Tuesday, Dec. 12' - matches), 2024-07-30 Tue, 2024-11-05 Tue, 2026-07-21 Tue. Cross-check: the six-seat + mayor + vice-mayor model reproduces all eight ACFR 'Principal Officials' snapshots (FY2018-FY2025) with zero unexplained persons and zero unfilled seats. Name-variant traps handled rather than merged: the ACFRs render Mathews as both 'Michael Mathews' and 'Michael Matthews', Hulse as 'Dough Hulse' (FY2021) and 'Doub Hulse' (FY2022), Palosaari as 'Derek Polassari', DuVernay as 'Lisa DuVerney' and (in a headline) 'DuVernary', Wilden as 'Deb Wilden' and 'Debbie Wilden', Dowell as 'Christoper Dowell' on the city's own candidate page. Winning-is-not-holding check applied to Stephen DeWillis: he was a write-in in the 2022-08-02 primary with 147 votes against a 129-vote threshold to reach the November ballot, so the primary alone does not seat him - his tenure is sourced to the FY2023 ACFR, which names him as a seated council member.

SEAT-LABEL CAVEAT (not a gap). Cottonwood's council is at-large and unnumbered, so 'which seat' is a modelling construct, not a fact on the ballot. Seats A/B/C are the class elected 2018/2022/2026 and D/E/F the class elected 2016/2020/2024. Two people legitimately change class within the panel because Arizona fills an unexpired term at the next regular election: Jackie Nairn was appointed 2019 to the remainder of Kyla Allen's 2018-2022 term (Seat A) and then won a full four-year term in 2020 (Seat F), while Debbie Wilden was appointed 2019 to Deb Althouse's 2016-2020 term (Seat F) and then won the TWO-YEAR term on the 2020 ballot (Seat A) before winning a full term in 2022. Both therefore have two tenure rows under two labels in 2020; the dates do not overlap. Confirmed by the 2020 results, which list three four-year seats (Henry, Nairn, Kurot) and a separate uncontested two-year council term (Wilden).

Soft boundary dates, recorded here rather than as gaps because the affected seat-years are all sourced. (a) Vice Mayor designation dates are not individually sourced except Allen (Jan 2018) and Hulse (2022-01-04 roll call); the other holders are pinned to the ACFR snapshot date on which they are named as Vice Mayor, so the handover boundaries within FY are approximate - hence medium confidence. Felicia Coates's Vice Mayor start is the only low-confidence row in the file: she is named Vice Mayor in the FY2025 ACFR and on the current council page, and the new council was seated in early December 2024, but no source fixes the designation date, so 2025-01-01 is used and 2024 is credited to Wilden. (b) Jackie Nairn's resignation date is given as 2023-09-30 (medium): the Verde Independent reported on 2023-10-01 that ten people had applied for the vacancy, so she left before that, but no source states the day. (c) Sub-year vacancies at 2019-03-01..03-10, 2019-11-01..12-05, 2023-04-01..06-05 and 2023-10..12-11 are real but do not create uncovered seat-years and so are not filed as gaps.
64 seat-years (8 offices x 8 years, 2019-2026) all covered by at least one tenure row. Zero gaps. Zero unrecovered cycles.
